title: Haapsalu lace shawl knitting
summary: In the Estonian seaside town of Haapsalu, knitters have long made gossamer shawls from fine wool, with open leaf and diamond lace, eyelets made by yarn-overs and tiny raised knots called nupps. The finished shawl is pinned out damp so the pattern opens, and the finest can be drawn through a ring.
howToPlay: Study the chart on the reference card: each motif is a stitch and each tone a yarn.
Choose a yarn tone and a lace stitch, then place it on the shawl; the quarter-turn partners are knitted too.
Press Check to compare your lace with the chart and see where stitches need mending.
rules: The chart repeats under quarter turns, so every stitch you place is mirrored by three partners.
Each cell holds one lace stitch in one yarn tone.
Leaves, eyelets, diamonds and nupps must match the chart in place, stitch and tone.
Your match is the share of stitches that agree with the chart; three stars need nearly a perfect copy.
heritageNote: Haapsalu shawls date from the early nineteenth century in Estonia's western coastal town of Haapsalu, where guild knitters keep the craft alive today.
